problems: dsa/heap still has IMPLEMENTED=false, so `new BinaryHeap()` would throw NotImplementedError on the first lease grant. I followed the repo's existing pattern (kernel/src/host/timers.ts, kernel proc table, klog): ExpiryIndex uses dsa/heap when HEAP_IMPLEMENTED is true and otherwise a built-in Map with a linear-scan minimum. That stand-in is not a heap, and it carries a TODO(dsa/heap) to delete it. Tests cover both the heap path (a test-only IndexedMinHeap double) and the stand-in. The broadcaster's per-owner hold list reuses the same index.

The spec wants conflicted-copy names from the isomorphic vfs/names.ts and the subtree digest from vfs/digest.ts. The server boundary (tools/eslint-rules/boundaries.js) and vfs/package.json exports allow only @plotinium/vfs/path and /perm. So engine/sync/names.ts (conflictName, isoDate) and base-check.ts subtreeDigest are line-for-line mirrors, marked TODO(boundary) and pinned by tests.

server/src/vfs/types.ts VfsCall has no 'utimes', 'audit.append' or 'session.layout'. Those op kinds currently get `retry ENOSYS not-implemented` (retryAfterMs 60 s), so clients keep them rather than losing them. The same answer applies to any op kind that has no handler: only `write` is implemented here, and create/unlink/rename/link/copy/chmod/chown/batch come from the vfs/ops handlers.

§3.12.5 server-side salvage of REJECTED content (EACCES, EPERM, parent ENOENT) into ~/lost+found is not implemented, because it needs a hook inside vfsTxn's recordRejection transaction (server/src/vfs, not my path). The client parks the bytes locally instead (§3.12.4), so nothing is lost.
A duplicate of a retention-pruned tombstone can only report `pruned: true` if the stored result says so, because vfsTxn's readStoredOp does not return purged_at.
GET /api/sync/snapshot (the target of snapshot.required) was not in my assignment and is not implemented. The frame and its URL are produced: /api/sync/snapshot?scope=owner&owner=<uid>.

LockNotifier.watchersOf (lock.released pushed to connections watching the file's directory) is not wired, because it needs a parent lookup. Connections that were denied or queued for an inode are notified by the manager itself.
